Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Row was mislabelled as Unknown/no-source; a single light check surfaced an authoritative primary source, so it was moved to full verification. The NRA eTax platform (etax.nra.gov.ss) has been mandatory for tax declaration and filing since 1 July 2021 (NRA Official Circular, July 2021; corroborated by EY TaxNews and Eye Radio). The NRA eTax Filing & Declaration Manual confirms that on filing, taxpayers generate an invoice which can be paid online by card (immediately or later) or taken to an integrated bank — i.e. direct online e-payment capability exists alongside filing. Original score of 0/Unknown corrected to 4=Yes.
revised_comments: South Sudan's National Revenue Authority (NRA) operates the eTax platform (etax.nra.gov.ss), which has been mandatory for all taxpayers — citizens, foreign residents, businesses and NGOs — for declaring and filing tax returns since 1 July 2021. The platform generates a tax invoice on filing, which can be paid online by card (immediately or later) or settled at an integrated bank, giving the portal direct e-payment capability alongside its filing function.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A fast-path search surfaced substantive material, so the row was moved to full path. South Sudan does not appear as a live or extended-network participant in PAPSS (per PAPSS's June 2026 network coverage list). The domestic National Instant Payment System (SSIPSS/ATS+, combining RTGS and ACH) launched 10 October 2025 (Eye Radio), and South Sudan joined the EAC-PSSIP project (AfDB, 2019) with the eventual aim of connecting to the East African Payment System (EAPS), a requirement of EAC membership. However, the 2023 UNCDF/IGAD payment infrastructure assessment states that cross-border/regional hub participation is a future precursor step, not yet concretely planned, pending resolution of domestic interoperability gaps. Private mobile money cross-border interoperability exists informally (m-Gurush with MTN Uganda and Safaricom Kenya) but sits outside the government instant payment system and does not count toward this variable. Recalculated from 0/Unknown to 2=Planned; flagged for human review given the informal, loosely-dated sourcing on any concrete timeline.
revised_comments: South Sudan's national instant payment system (SSIPSS), launched in October 2025 by the Bank of South Sudan, is not yet connected to any cross-border payment scheme, and the country is not a participant (direct, indirect or extended network) in the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS). As an East African Community member, South Sudan is expected eventually to connect to the East African Payment System (EAPS) through the EAC Payment and Settlement Systems Integration Project, but regional/cross-border functionality remains a stated future ambition rather than an active work stream, with domestic interoperability prioritised first. Private mobile money interoperability (for example, m-Gurush with MTN Uganda and Safaricom Kenya) provides limited informal cross-border transfer capability outside the government payment system.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: No specific payment consumer protection/dispute framework found.

revision_notes: A fast-path search surfaced an authoritative regulatory action, so the row was moved to full path. The Bank of South Sudan issued a regulatory notice (reported September 2025) explicitly extending consumer protection requirements to mobile money operators and electronic payment platforms, covering disclosure of loan/fee terms, data protection, prohibitions on aggressive fee/debt-collection practices, mandatory complaint/dispute-resolution channels, and sanctions (including licence suspension) for breaches. This sits alongside the general Consumer Protection Act 2011, which is not payment-specific. Recalculated from 0/Unknown to 3=Yes; flagged for human review because this rests on a detailed secondary news report of the regulatory notice rather than the primary BoSS circular text, which should be sourced directly to confirm scope and legal status.
revised_comments: The Bank of South Sudan's 2025 regulatory notice on banks, microfinance institutions and digital financial service providers extends specific consumer protection requirements to digital payment services, including disclosure of fees and repayment terms, data protection and cyber-security obligations, prohibitions on aggressive or fraudulent fee practices, and mandatory customer complaint and dispute-resolution channels, backed by sanctions including licence suspension for non-compliance. This sits alongside the general Consumer Protection Act 2011, which established a Consumer Protection Council and court/complaint enforcement mechanisms but does not address payment services specifically.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: No breach notif requirements found after searches.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A fast-path search surfaced a clear primary legislative source, so the row was moved to full path. The Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Act 2026, signed into law by President Salva Kiir on 18 February 2026, designates banking and financial services as eligible 'critical national infrastructure' (Section 26) and mandates (Section 30) that owners of designated critical infrastructure report any cybersecurity incident to the authority within 24 hours of detection, alongside a duty to conduct regular audits. This is corroborated independently by Radio Tamazuj's legal explainer and the Internet Society South Sudan Chapter analysis. A September 2025 BoSS regulatory notice separately required digital financial service providers to strengthen cyber defences and data protection, though it did not specify a breach-notification timeframe. Recalculated from 0/Unknown to 3=Mandatory, noting the requirement applies once a payment system/financial entity is formally designated as critical infrastructure under the Act.
revised_comments: The Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Act 2026, signed into law on 18 February 2026, requires owners of computer systems and networks designated as critical national infrastructure — a category that explicitly includes banking and financial services — to report any cybersecurity incident, including data breaches, to the national authority within 24 hours of detection, and to submit regular audit reports. This mandatory notification duty is enforced through administrative penalties for non-compliance and sits alongside a September 2025 Bank of South Sudan directive requiring digital financial service providers to strengthen data protection and cyber-security controls.
